question: Which blood cells help in clotting of blood and stop bleeding?

options.text: Both platelets and red blood cells

solution:
The correct answer is __**platelets**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Blood is a body fluid **in humans and other animals that delivers necessary substances such as nutrients and oxygen to the cells and transports metabolic waste products away from those same cells.
 
• **Platelets are also known as thrombocytes.**
 
• Platelets **are tiny blood cells that help your body form clots to stop bleeding.**
 
• If one of your blood vessels gets damaged, it sends out signals to the platelets.
 
• **The platelets then rush to the site of damage and form a plug (clot) to fix the damage**.
 
• The process of spreading across the surface of a damaged blood vessel to stop bleeding is called adhesion.
 
• This is because when platelets get to the site of the injury, they grow sticky tentacles that help them stick (adhere) to one another.
 
• They also send out chemical signals to attract more platelets.
 
• The **additional platelets pile onto the clot in a process called aggregation.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bf2f2df5e48a87da371f3a75ff65214cfdd97a7212abba76f9d1a6a7c8500113.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/10cd5297625876c19405b4c8b0df9fb091d5ca53994f304a79d0d2f4e50304c2.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Human** blood is composed of blood cells and blood plasma.**
 
• **Blood cells consist of erythrocytes (RBC), leukocytes (WBC**).
 
• The **function** of RBC is to distribute oxygen to each cell of the body.
 
• **WBC are responsible for the immune system of the bo**dy.
 
• White blood cells are further divided into eosinophil, basophil, monocyte, lymphocyte, and neutrophils.
 
• A monocyte is a type of white blood cell and a type of phagocyte.
